newsitem.title: USA: Viacom to offer Blockbuster tracking stock.
newsitem.headline: Viacom to offer Blockbuster tracking stock.

text.p: Viacom Inc said Tuesday it plans a public offering next year of a new class of Viacom stock that will track the performance of its Blockbuster Entertainment chain of video stores.
It also said Blockbuster Chairman and Chief Executive Bill Fields is resigning and a replacement will be named shortly.
Viacom said the public stock offering will represent "a minority of the new (stock) class."
"Viacom intends to retain a significant shareholding in the tracking stock," it said.

Viacom, a diversified entertainment company, said it sees a 15 to 20 percent fall in Blockbuster's first quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) compared to the 1996 first quarter. It blamed "inferior" video releases during the quarter and some temporary headaches due to a move of corporate headquarters from Fort Lauderdale to Dallas.
Viacom said it "remains confident that Blockbuster will resume earnings growth in the second half of 1997."
Proceeds from sales of the new Viacom stock will be used to repay debt, Viacom said.

At year-end 1996, Blockbuster had more than 5,300 domestic and international video stores in 24 countries and about 500 music stores. Its video and music store operations had 1996 revenues of $3.54 billion and EBITDA of $775 million.

Sumner Redstone, Viacom chairman and chief executive, said, "Issuing a tracking stock will enable us to raise equity capital to reduce our debt, will provide an attractive opportunity for investors interested in Blockbuster, and will make it possible for shareholders to better capture the value of all of Viacom's businesses ... The implementation of this strategy will leave Viacom with a great deal of financial flexibility."
Until a new Blockbuster chief is selected, Blockbuster's operations will report to Redstone and Viacom Deputy Chairman Tom Dooley, Viacom said.
